Maharashtra Farmers’ Protest Blocks NH-48, Strands 1,500 Trucks

Outlook News Desk
Curated by: Aryan Dwivedi
Published at: 6 November 2026 12:38 pm

The blockade has disrupted bus services as well. The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) has cancelled around 100 trips daily.

Prefer on Google
Outlook News Desk
Curated by: Aryan Dwivedi
Published at: 6 November 2026 12:38 pm
Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana activists and farmers sit on the road and eat meals during their ongoing protest demanding higher sugarcane prices, blockading the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway (NH-48) at Kini toll plaza, in Kolhapur district, Maharashtra. | Photo: PTI
Summary of this article

  • The Pune-Bengaluru highway remained blocked for a third day as farmers demanded a ₹4,500-per-tonne advance for sugarcane.

  • The protest disrupted traffic across a 120-km stretch, leaving heavy vehicles stranded and clogging diversion routes.

  • MSRTC cancelled around 100 bus trips daily; transporters said more than 1,500 trucks carrying goods were stuck.

The Pune-Bengaluru National Highway (NH-48) remained blocked for a third consecutive day on Thursday as farmers led by former MP Raju Shetti continued their agitation for an advance payment of ₹4,500 per tonne of sugarcane.

The blockade has disrupted traffic along nearly 120 km between Nagthane in Satara district and Sangli Phata in Kolhapur district. Heavy vehicles remained stranded, while traffic diverted onto bypasses and smaller roads caused congestion across the region. Commuters travelling towards Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara and Belagavi were affected.

“We have been stuck on the highway since last night with our children and elderly family members. We were travelling to Kolhapur to celebrate Diwali with our relatives, but our vehicle has barely moved for hours. We have limited food and water, and the children are getting restless,” said Mangesh Chirute, a passenger stranded on the highway, as reported by Hinudstan Times.

Ethanol, Sugar Prices And Drought: Why Maharashtra’s Farmers Are Protesting

By Outlook News Desk

Diversions Push Traffic Onto Smaller Roads

Vehicles travelling from Pune towards Kolhapur and Sangli faced heavy congestion between the D-Mart area in Satara and Ajintha Chowk. Authorities diverted traffic through Rahimatpur, but heavy trucks on the alternative route slowed movement further and made it difficult for smaller vehicles to pass.

Small vehicles heading towards Sangli have been advised to travel through Satara city and take the Rahimatpur route, then continue via Pusesavali and Palus. Motorists going to Kolhapur can use routes through Rahimatpur, including roads connecting Ashta in Sangli district, Bagani and Peth Vadgaon. These routes are also facing increasing pressure, and authorities have urged commuters to check road conditions before setting out.

Ethanol Blending in Petrol to Remain at 20%, Says Hardeep Puri

By Outlook News Desk

MSRTC Cancels About 100 Trips A Day

The blockade has disrupted bus services as well. The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) has cancelled around 100 trips daily.

“We had already started operating some buses through alternative routes from Wednesday, including via Sangli, Rahimatpur and Vita, to ensure that passengers stranded on the way could reach their destinations,” said Arun Siya, MSRTC Pune divisional controller.

“We are constantly assessing which routes can safely be used to operate services and hope that a solution will emerge soon,” he said.

The diversion routes have also raised safety concerns. Siya said a Karnataka-registered bus was stopped near Rahimatpur, beyond Satara, on Thursday and its window panes were damaged.

Trucks Carrying Essential Goods Remain Stranded

The protest has held up commercial transport and deliveries of essential goods. More than 1,500 trucks carrying grains, vegetables and other commodities have been stranded for two days, said Baba Shinde, president of the Maharashtra State Transporters Association.

“The prolonged blockade is causing major losses to transporters and could also affect the supply chain if the situation continues,” Shinde told Hindustan Times

Farmers Seek Higher Cane Payment

The Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana is demanding a minimum first instalment of ₹4,500 per tonne for sugarcane supplied to mills during the current crushing season. It says mills earn substantial revenue from sugar, ethanol and other by-products but do not share a fair proportion with growers.

The organisation has also sought an increase in the minimum selling price of sugar from ₹31 to ₹50 per kg and a revision of ethanol procurement prices. It has warned that it will intensify the agitation if farmers and sugar factories fail to reach an agreement.

As BJP-Shinde Rift Widens, Fadnavis Shares Stage With Thackeray Brothers: Maharashtra Politics In For A Twist?

By Pranay Vatsa

Fadnavis Urges Farmers To End Agitation

Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has appealed to farmers to call off the protest peacefully. He said the government fixes the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP), while payments above that rate must be negotiated between sugar factories and farmers.

Fadnavis said Minister Hasan Mushrif had been asked to hold talks with stakeholders. Discussions involving sugar industry representatives and experts are also expected at the Sugar Commissioner’s office in Pune.

Farmers, commuters and transport operators are awaiting a settlement as negotiations continue and the highway remains disrupted.

	<div class="entry-content">
		
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Andhra Pradesh Lorry Owners’ Association (APLOA) has asked the Union Finance Ministry and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) to step in over the reported detention of more than 300 trucks at the Assam–West Bengal border. The association says the consignments carry valid GST documents and that Integrated GST (IGST) has been paid on them.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The trucks are carrying raw petroleum coke (RPC), a refinery by-product, from Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) refineries at Bongaigaon, Guwahati and Digboi in Assam. The vehicles have reportedly been held around Srirampur and Bakshirhat since September 17.</p><div class="code-block code-block-1" style="margin: 8px auto; text-align: center; display: block; clear: both;">
<div id="p-tag3" class=""> 
<!--?xml encoding="utf-8" ?--><!-- Ad space powered by WP AdCenter v2.5.7 - https://wpadcenter.com/ --><div class="wpadcenter-ad-container"><div id="wpadcenter-ad-38964" class="ad-350x300 wpadcenter-350x300 ad-placement  wpadcenter-alignnone alignnone"><div class="wpadcenter-ad-inner wpadcenter-gapi" data="posts after 2 paragraph:38964"><a id="wpadcenter_ad" data-value="38964" data-placement="" href="https://www.vantagesummit.in/participate/" target="_blank" class="wpadcenter-ad-inner__item"><img width="973" height="834" src="https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Vantage-Web-Banner-800-X-800-copy-1.webp" class="attachment-post-thumbnail size-post-thumbnail wp-post-image" alt="" srcset="https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Vantage-Web-Banner-800-X-800-copy-1.webp 973w, https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Vantage-Web-Banner-800-X-800-copy-1-300x257.webp 300w, https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Vantage-Web-Banner-800-X-800-copy-1-768x658.webp 768w, https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Vantage-Web-Banner-800-X-800-copy-1-600x514.webp 600w" sizes="(max-width: 973px) 100vw, 973px"></a></div></div></div>
</div>
</div>




<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Where the cargo is headed</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">APLOA general secretary Y.V. Eswara Rao said nearly half the trucks were carrying consignments for Visakhapatnam. The rest were bound for Haldia and Durgapur in West Bengal, Barauni in Bihar and Paradip in Odisha.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">APLOA wants authorities to verify 16 trucks carrying RPC for Rain CII Carbon (Vizag) Ltd, based on a vehicle list from IOC’s Marketing division, Eastern Region, and to release them if they are being held without lawful grounds. As an example, it cited an e-way bill for truck AP39VW-1447, which records a taxable value of ₹17.28 lakh and IGST of ₹3.11 lakh at 18%. The consignment was invoiced by IOC, Assam, to Rain CII Carbon (Vizag), with Shiva Transport Agency as the transporter.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">The cost of standing still</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">APLOA estimates demurrage and related losses for transporters and other stakeholders at about ₹1 crore. It warns that further delays could disrupt production and raise logistics costs for consignors and consignees.</p><div class="code-block code-block-2" style="margin: 8px auto; text-align: center; display: block; clear: both;">
<div id="p-tag5" class="">
<!--?xml encoding="utf-8" ?--><!-- Ad space powered by WP AdCenter v2.5.7 - https://wpadcenter.com/ --><div class="wpadcenter-ad-container"><div id="wpadcenter-ad-38968" class="ad-350x300 wpadcenter-350x300 ad-placement  wpadcenter-alignnone alignnone"><div class="wpadcenter-ad-inner wpadcenter-gapi" data="Posts After 5 Paragraph:38968"><a id="wpadcenter_ad" data-value="38968" data-placement="" href="https://www.bobbagroup.com" target="_blank" class="wpadcenter-ad-inner__item"><img width="350" height="300" src="https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/BE-banner-350x300-1.webp" class="attachment-post-thumbnail size-post-thumbnail wp-post-image" alt="" srcset="https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/BE-banner-350x300-1.webp 350w, https://www.logisticsinsider.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/BE-banner-350x300-1-300x257.webp 300w" sizes="(max-width: 350px) 100vw, 350px"></a></div></div></div>
</div>

</div>




<p class="wp-block-paragraph">P. Venkata Siva Nagaraju, a truck owner from Vijayawada, said three of his newly acquired trucks had been held at an outpost on the West Bengal border for more than a month.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The association accepts that valid papers do not exempt cargo from lawful inspection, but says prolonged detention must rest on stated legal grounds. It has sought disclosure of any written orders, better coordination among GST authorities in the states concerned and uniform procedures for vehicles carrying valid documents.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">"Orders from above"</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Transporters have alleged that police and GST officials on the ground cited only “orders from above” and served no written order. Some transporters have linked the stoppage to West Bengal’s crackdown on illegal coal transport, arguing RPC is a refinery by-product, not mined coal. The Barauni Calciners Association said earlier this month that West Bengal’s commercial taxes commissioner had assured it the matter was resolved, but the trucks were not allowed through. No official explanation from West Bengal authorities has been reported.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The standoff comes as the GST Council has recommended curbs on transit-state checks. Under the <a href="https://www.logisticsinsider.in/gst-council-eases-transit-checks-senior-officer-approval-now-mandatory-random-highway-inspections-curbed/">proposed changes</a>, goods in transit may be inspected, detained or seized only by officers of the state where the supplier or recipient is located, and not by transit states. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on October 8 that goods cannot be stopped in between.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">MUNDRA: Container movement at <strong><a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/tag/mundra-port/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Mundra Port</a></strong> has come under significant pressure following a strike by empty-container yard operators, with industry estimates suggesting that around 5,000 containers a day are being held up amid disruptions to the return, storage and repositioning of empty boxes.</p>


<div class="wp-block-image">
<figure class="alignleft size-full is-resized"><a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/trade-notice-mundra-strike.jpg" class="td-modal-image"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="527" height="800" src="https://indiashippingnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/trade-notice-mundra-strike.jpg" alt="trade notice mundra strike Mundra Container Yard strike disrupts EXIM supply chain as around 5,000 containers a day face delays" class="wp-image-95398" style="width:375px;height:auto" title="Mundra Container Yard strike disrupts EXIM supply chain as around 5,000 containers a day face delays 1 Mundra Container Yard strike disrupts EXIM supply chain as around 5,000 containers a day face delays"></a></figure>
</div>


<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The disruption follows a decision by <strong>Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (<a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/tag/apsez/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">APSEZ</a>)</strong> to freeze empty-yard codes for facilities located outside the <strong>Mundra Port</strong> and<strong> SEZ </strong>limits from September 1, 2026. Under the revised arrangement, shipping lines are required to nominate empty containers to designated yards operating within the Mundra Port SEZ.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The decision has triggered strong opposition from external empty-container yard operators, who suspended services in protest, leading to a wider disruption across the container logistics chain.</p><div class="td-a-ad id_inline_ad0 id_ad_content-horiz-center"><span class="td-adspot-title"></span><!-- /23371410655/news_incontent_1 -->
<div id="div-gpt-ad-1788421279432-0" style="min-width: 300px; min-height: 250px; display: none;" data-google-query-id="CPOA4Jiim5gDFZvAcgkdTOEIGg">

<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Exporters Face Shortage of Empty Containers</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">One of the most immediate impacts has been on exporters dependent on empty containers for factory stuffing. With affected yards suspending operations, the availability and release of empty containers for export cargo has been disrupted.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">At the same time, importers and transporters are facing difficulties in returning empty containers after cargo de-stuffing, creating congestion and delays across the logistics network.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The situation has raised concerns over missed vessel cut-offs, shipment rollovers and potential additional costs for exporters and importers if the disruption continues.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Several major shipping lines have issued customer advisories regarding the operational challenges. MSC and Ocean Network Express (ONE) have advised customers to review their export plans and make alternative arrangements where possible to minimise potential delays. Other carriers have also highlighted restrictions affecting empty-container releases and returns at impacted facilities.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Transporters Join the Disruption</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The situation has further intensified with container <a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/news/transport/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">transporters</a> extending support to the striking empty-yard operators. Reports indicate that a large number of transporters serving the Mundra logistics ecosystem have halted or restricted container movements, adding further pressure to the already disrupted supply chain.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This has widened the impact beyond empty-container yards, affecting the movement of containers between factories, container freight stations, depots and port terminals.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">However, some logistics activities continue to remain operational. Cargo stuffing and gate-in operations through Container Freight Stations (CFSs) have continued, providing exporters with an alternative route for moving cargo through Mundra, although factory stuffing operations remain among the most affected segments.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Different Views Over the New Empty Container System</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" href="https://www.adaniports.com/">APSEZ</a> has maintained that the new arrangement is aimed at creating a more integrated empty-container management system within the Mundra ecosystem.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">According to the company’s stated objectives, the move is expected to help reduce road congestion, improve truck turnaround times, shorten container movements, enhance safety and security controls and reduce emissions associated with longer road movements.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">However, external depot operators and sections of the logistics community have raised concerns about the sudden impact of the transition on existing <a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/news/container/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">container</a> handling arrangements.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Industry stakeholders argue that shipping lines require operational flexibility in deciding where their empty containers are stored, inspected, repaired and positioned for future export movements.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The dispute has therefore developed into a broader issue involving port operations, empty-container depots, shipping lines, transporters, customs brokers and exporters.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Trade Bodies Seek Urgent Resolution</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The disruption has prompted calls from industry bodies for an early resolution to prevent further impact on India’s <a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/news/export-import/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">export-import</a> trade.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Customs brokers and freight forwarders have expressed concerns over additional logistics costs, stranded vehicles, delays in container returns and the risk of exporters missing planned vessel sailings.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Stakeholders have also sought measures to ensure that importers and exporters are not burdened with detention charges or other additional costs arising from circumstances beyond their control.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">With Mundra serving as one of India’s most important gateways for containerised trade, a prolonged disruption could affect supply chains serving manufacturing and export centres across Gujarat and northern and western India.</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Focus Turns to Restoration of Normal Container Flows</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The key challenge now is restoring the seamless circulation of empty containers between importers, depots, factories, CFS facilities and port terminals.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The empty container is a critical link in the export supply chain. Any disruption in its availability can quickly affect factory stuffing schedules, inland transport planning and vessel connections.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">As discussions continue among port authorities, depot operators, <a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/news/shipping-line/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">shipping lines</a> and trade stakeholders, the industry will be closely watching for a resolution that can restore normal container flows while addressing concerns surrounding the new empty-container management system.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">For now, exporters and importers moving cargo through Mundra are being advised to closely monitor carrier advisories, review shipment schedules and coordinate with shipping lines and <a href="https://indiashippingnews.com/news/logistics/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">logistics</a> partners to reduce the risk of operational delays.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>

            <!-- content --><p class="isSelectedEnd">A strike is disrupting empty container yard operations connected to Mundra Port in India, according to Hapag-Lloyd.</p>
<p class="isSelectedEnd">Until further notice, the affected empty container yards have suspended:</p>
<ul data-spread="false">
<li>Empty container allotments for factory stuffing</li>
<li>Empty container gate-ins</li>
</ul>
<h2>CFS operations remain unaffected</h2>
<p class="isSelectedEnd">Container Freight Station operations at Mundra Port continue normally. Customers can therefore continue using:</p>
<ul data-spread="false">
<li>CFS stuffing operations</li>
<li>CFS gate-ins</li>
</ul>
<p class="isSelectedEnd">Hapag-Lloyd advised customers planning export shipments through Mundra Port to review their arrangements. Exporters should consider the current restrictions on empty container availability and movements.</p>
<p>The carrier said it is monitoring the situation and remains in contact with the relevant stakeholders. It will provide another update when normal operations resume or further information becomes available.</p>

However, they said their protest would continue until the Union government announces a revised Minimum Selling Price (MSP) for sugar and a higher Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane. The ongoing agitation at the Kognoli toll plaza on the Mumbai-Bengaluru National Highway 48 (NH-48) has disrupted traffic, prompting Maharashtra Police to advise motorists to take alternative routes.The farmers are demanding a revision of the MSP of sugar to Rs 60 per kg and an increase in the FRP to Rs 5,500 per tonne of sugarcane. The current FRP fixed by Union government is Rs 3,650 per tonne.Their other demands include transparency in weighing and sugar recovery assessments at factories, increased procurement of ethanol produced from sugarcane and maize in Karnataka, and differential pricing for sugar sold to domestic and industrial consumers.Farmers are also seeking legislation to make themselves shareholders in public, cooperative, and private sugar factories, with a share in profits from sugar and by-products such as molasses, ethanol, co-generated power, oxygen, bio-fertiliser, and press mud. Other demands include government-supervised installation and monitoring of computerised weighing scales and a statewide sugarcane harvesting and transportation calendar to be enforced by district administrations.Chunappa Pujeri, a farmer leader associated with the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha (KRRS) and Hasiru Sene in the Belagavi and Chikkodi regions, told reporters at Mukti Mathi near Belagavi on October 15 that farmers welcomed the formation of a committee headed by agriculture scientist Ramesh Chand to examine their demands. However, he said the protest would continue until the Union government announces an MSP of at least Rs 60 per kg of sugar and an FRP of Rs 5,500 per tonne of sugarcane.“It is good that the committee has representation of all stakeholders. It has been told to look into MSP, FRP, and all related issues. We hope the committee gives its report soon, and that the Union Government implements it. However, this is no reason for us to withdraw the protest,” Pujeri said.Farmers’ leader Shashikant Padasalagi Guruji questioned the government’s reluctance to revise the prices, arguing that separate rates could be fixed for sugar meant for domestic consumption and for industrial use.“What is the price of sugar in the market now? Is the government not selling domestic and commercial LPG cylinders at different rates? Why can it not fix separate prices for domestic consumption of sugar and those bought by industrial houses? Why does the government want to keep farmers poor in the name of keeping food prices under control?” he asked.Raju Shetty, leader of the Maharashtra Shetkari Sanghatan, said members of his organisation would join the Hubballi Chalo Padayatra from Kolhapur and neighbouring areas in solidarity with Karnataka’s sugarcane farmers.Karnataka Minister criticises Union government over talksKarnataka Cooperation Minister Laxman Savadi criticised the Union government over its handling of the farmers’ demands, saying Union ministers appeared unprepared during a meeting with farmers’ representatives in New Delhi on October 12.Savadi, who attended the meeting along with Karnataka Sugar Minister Rudrappa Lamani, said Union ministers Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Pralhad Joshi should have arrived with clarity on whether the MSP for sugar and the FRP for sugarcane could be revised.“I am disappointed with the Union government,” Savadi told reporters in Chikkodi on October 15.He said the meeting had yielded no immediate decision, with the Union government instead proposing to form a committee within a week, obtain its recommendations in about a month, and take a final decision on revising the prices later.“There was no sense of urgency in any of them. I felt, just like several other farmers’ leaders, that their response to the problems of sugarcane farmers was not appropriate,” he said.NH-48 traffic disrupted at Kognoli toll plazaMeanwhile, the ongoing protest at the Kognoli toll plaza in Karnataka disrupted traffic on NH-48 on the morning of Wednesday, October 14, affecting vehicles travelling towards Belagavi and Bengaluru.NH-48 is a key interstate corridor connecting Mumbai and Pune with Bengaluru and other industrial centres in southern India. The disruption has inconvenienced motorists, bus passengers, and transport operators travelling towards Karnataka.In an advisory issued on Wednesday, the Maharashtra Highway Police said the situation remained unchanged from Tuesday evening and advised motorists travelling from Mumbai towards Bengaluru to avoid NH-48 as far as possible until further instructions.Inspector General of Police for the Kolhapur range Ranjan Kumar Sharma appealed to commuters to use alternative routes through Satara, Sangli, and Kolhapur districts.The farmers have maintained that the agitation will continue until the Union government announces a decision on revising the prices, despite the formation of the committee. .Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links.","dateCreated":"2026-10-16T04:13:26Z","dateModified":"2026-10-16T04:13:23Z","name":"Karnataka sugarcane farmers hold firm on MSP, FRP demands as Union govt sets up panel","inLanguage":"en","isPartOf":{"@type":"WebPage","url":"https://www.thenewsminute.com/karnataka/karnataka-sugarcane-farmers-hold-firm-on-msp-frp-demands-as-union-govt-sets-up-panel","primaryImageOfPage":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://cf-images.assettype.com/thenewsminute/2026-10-16/ixzq6y8f/Sugarcane-farmers?w=1200&h=675&auto=format%2Ccompress&fit=max&enlarge=true","width":"1200","height":"675"}},"articleSection":"Karnataka","alternativeHeadline":""}</script>

text-m_dark__1TC18 "><p>Sugarcane farmers in Karnataka have welcomed the Union government’s decision to set up a four-member committee to examine their demands. However, they said their protest would continue until the Union government announces a revised Minimum Selling Price (MSP) for sugar and a higher Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane. The ongoing agitation at the Kognoli toll plaza on the Mumbai-Bengaluru National Highway 48 (NH-48) has disrupted traffic, prompting Maharashtra Police to advise motorists to take alternative routes.</p><p>The farmers are demanding a revision of the MSP of sugar to Rs 60 per kg and an increase in the FRP to Rs 5,500 per tonne of sugarcane. The current FRP fixed by Union government is Rs 3,650 per tonne.</p><p>Their other demands include transparency in weighing and sugar recovery assessments at factories, increased procurement of ethanol produced from sugarcane and maize in Karnataka, and differential pricing for sugar sold to domestic and industrial consumers.</p><p>Farmers are also seeking legislation to make themselves shareholders in public, cooperative, and private sugar factories, with a share in profits from sugar and by-products such as molasses, ethanol, co-generated power, oxygen, bio-fertiliser, and press mud. Other demands include government-supervised installation and monitoring of computerised weighing scales and a statewide sugarcane harvesting and transportation calendar to be enforced by district administrations.</p><p>Chunappa Pujeri, a farmer leader associated with the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha (KRRS) and Hasiru Sene in the Belagavi and Chikkodi regions, told reporters at Mukti Mathi near Belagavi on October 15 that farmers welcomed the formation of a committee headed by agriculture scientist Ramesh Chand to examine their demands. However, he said the protest would continue until the Union government announces an MSP of at least Rs 60 per kg of sugar and an FRP of Rs 5,500 per tonne of sugarcane.</p><p>“It is good that the committee has representation of all stakeholders. It has been told to look into MSP, FRP, and all related issues. We hope the committee gives its report soon, and that the Union Government implements it. However, this is no reason for us to withdraw the protest,” Pujeri said.</p><p>Farmers’ leader Shashikant Padasalagi Guruji questioned the government’s reluctance to revise the prices, arguing that separate rates could be fixed for sugar meant for domestic consumption and for industrial use.</p><p>“What is the price of sugar in the market now? Is the government not selling domestic and commercial LPG cylinders at different rates? Why can it not fix separate prices for domestic consumption of sugar and those bought by industrial houses? Why does the government want to keep farmers poor in the name of keeping food prices under control?” he asked.</p><p>Raju Shetty, leader of the Maharashtra Shetkari Sanghatan, said members of his organisation would join the Hubballi Chalo Padayatra from Kolhapur and neighbouring areas in solidarity with Karnataka’s sugarcane farmers.</p><h3><strong>Karnataka Minister criticises Union government over talks</strong></h3><p>Karnataka Cooperation Minister Laxman Savadi criticised the Union government over its handling of the farmers’ demands, saying Union ministers appeared unprepared during a meeting with farmers’ representatives in New Delhi on October 12.</p><p>Savadi, who attended the meeting along with Karnataka Sugar Minister Rudrappa Lamani, said Union ministers Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Pralhad Joshi should have arrived with clarity on whether the MSP for sugar and the FRP for sugarcane could be revised.</p><p>“I am disappointed with the Union government,” Savadi told reporters in Chikkodi on October 15.</p><p>He said the meeting had yielded no immediate decision, with the Union government instead proposing to form a committee within a week, obtain its recommendations in about a month, and take a final decision on revising the prices later.</p><p>“There was no sense of urgency in any of them. I felt, just like several other farmers’ leaders, that their response to the problems of sugarcane farmers was not appropriate,” he said.</p><h3><strong>NH-48 traffic disrupted at Kognoli toll plaza</strong></h3><p>Meanwhile, the ongoing protest at the Kognoli toll plaza in Karnataka disrupted traffic on NH-48 on the morning of Wednesday, October 14, affecting vehicles travelling towards Belagavi and Bengaluru.</p><p>NH-48 is a key interstate corridor connecting Mumbai and Pune with Bengaluru and other industrial centres in southern India. The disruption has inconvenienced motorists, bus passengers, and transport operators travelling towards Karnataka.</p><p>In an advisory issued on Wednesday, the Maharashtra Highway Police said the situation remained unchanged from Tuesday evening and advised motorists travelling from Mumbai towards Bengaluru to avoid NH-48 as far as possible until further instructions.</p><p>Inspector General of Police for the Kolhapur range Ranjan Kumar Sharma appealed to commuters to use alternative routes through Satara, Sangli, and Kolhapur districts.</p><p>The farmers have maintained that the agitation will continue until the Union government announces a decision on revising the prices, despite the formation of the committee.</p> </div></div><div class="arr--element-container However, they said their protest would continue until the Union government announces a revised Minimum Selling Price (MSP) for sugar and a higher Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane. The ongoing agitation at the Kognoli toll plaza on the Mumbai-Bengaluru National Highway 48 (NH-48) has disrupted traffic, prompting Maharashtra Police to advise motorists to take alternative routes.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe farmers are demanding a revision of the MSP of sugar to Rs 60 per kg and an increase in the FRP to Rs 5,500 per tonne of sugarcane. The current FRP fixed by Union government is Rs 3,650 per tonne.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETheir other demands include transparency in weighing and sugar recovery assessments at factories, increased procurement of ethanol produced from sugarcane and maize in Karnataka, and differential pricing for sugar sold to domestic and industrial consumers.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFarmers are also seeking legislation to make themselves shareholders in public, cooperative, and private sugar factories, with a share in profits from sugar and by-products such as molasses, ethanol, co-generated power, oxygen, bio-fertiliser, and press mud. Other demands include government-supervised installation and monitoring of computerised weighing scales and a statewide sugarcane harvesting and transportation calendar to be enforced by district administrations.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChunappa Pujeri, a farmer leader associated with the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha (KRRS) and Hasiru Sene in the Belagavi and Chikkodi regions, told reporters at Mukti Mathi near Belagavi on October 15 that farmers welcomed the formation of a committee headed by agriculture scientist Ramesh Chand to examine their demands. However, he said the protest would continue until the Union government announces an MSP of at least Rs 60 per kg of sugar and an FRP of Rs 5,500 per tonne of sugarcane.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“It is good that the committee has representation of all stakeholders. It has been told to look into MSP, FRP, and all related issues. We hope the committee gives its report soon, and that the Union Government implements it. However, this is no reason for us to withdraw the protest,” Pujeri said.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFarmers’ leader Shashikant Padasalagi Guruji questioned the government’s reluctance to revise the prices, arguing that separate rates could be fixed for sugar meant for domestic consumption and for industrial use.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“What is the price of sugar in the market now? Is the government not selling domestic and commercial LPG cylinders at different rates? Why can it not fix separate prices for domestic consumption of sugar and those bought by industrial houses? Why does the government want to keep farmers poor in the name of keeping food prices under control?” he asked.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERaju Shetty, leader of the Maharashtra Shetkari Sanghatan, said members of his organisation would join the Hubballi Chalo Padayatra from Kolhapur and neighbouring areas in solidarity with Karnataka’s sugarcane farmers.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Ch3\u003E\u003Cstrong\u003EKarnataka Minister criticises Union government over talks\u003C\u002Fstrong\u003E\u003C\u002Fh3\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKarnataka Cooperation Minister Laxman Savadi criticised the Union government over its handling of the farmers’ demands, saying Union ministers appeared unprepared during a meeting with farmers’ representatives in New Delhi on October 12.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESavadi, who attended the meeting along with Karnataka Sugar Minister Rudrappa Lamani, said Union ministers Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Pralhad Joshi should have arrived with clarity on whether the MSP for sugar and the FRP for sugarcane could be revised.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“I am disappointed with the Union government,” Savadi told reporters in Chikkodi on October 15.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe said the meeting had yielded no immediate decision, with the Union government instead proposing to form a committee within a week, obtain its recommendations in about a month, and take a final decision on revising the prices later.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003E“There was no sense of urgency in any of them. I felt, just like several other farmers’ leaders, that their response to the problems of sugarcane farmers was not appropriate,” he said.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Ch3\u003E\u003Cstrong\u003ENH-48 traffic disrupted at Kognoli toll plaza\u003C\u002Fstrong\u003E\u003C\u002Fh3\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMeanwhile, the ongoing protest at the Kognoli toll plaza in Karnataka disrupted traffic on NH-48 on the morning of Wednesday, October 14, affecting vehicles travelling towards Belagavi and Bengaluru.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENH-48 is a key interstate corridor connecting Mumbai and Pune with Bengaluru and other industrial centres in southern India. The disruption has inconvenienced motorists, bus passengers, and transport operators travelling towards Karnataka.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn an advisory issued on Wednesday, the Maharashtra Highway Police said the situation remained unchanged from Tuesday evening and advised motorists travelling from Mumbai towards Bengaluru to avoid NH-48 as far as possible until further instructions.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInspector General of Police for the Kolhapur range Ranjan Kumar Sharma appealed to commuters to use alternative routes through Satara, Sangli, and Kolhapur districts.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe farmers have maintained that the agitation will continue until the Union government announces a decision on revising the prices, despite the formation of the committee.\u003C\u002Fp\u003E     "articleBody" : "Bhubaneswar, Oct 8:  Normal life across Odisha was affected on Thursday due to the 12-hour statewide shutdown called by several opposition parties of the Congress-led INDIA bloc over four demands, including the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.The 12-hour shutdown disrupted transportation services across the state as members of the communist parties, Congress and other political parties blocked National and State Highways by burning tyres on the roads at various places.Workers and leaders of the INDIA bloc staged picketing at important places in cities across the state. Youth Congress members also held bike rallies during the bandh. Passenger buses, auto-rickshaws and trucks were largely off the roads due to the bandh.Train services were also affected at several places for a few hours, while scuffles between security personnel and the INDIA bloc workers and leaders were reported from some locations as the latter tried to halt train services at railway stations.Hundreds of vehicles remained stranded on highways, causing massive inconvenience to commuters. Private institutions, business establishments and other establishments in major cities across Odisha also remained closed due to the bandh.Speaking to media persons, Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee (OPCC) president Bhakta Charan Das on Thursday said the 12-hour Odisha bandh called by the INDIA bloc was being observed peacefully across the state, with people extending support to the shutdown.Das said the bandh was being observed over four key demands, which include the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, repeal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, resignation of Odisha School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in textbooks, and immediate relief and compensation for people affected by the recent floods in the state.“The impact of the bandh is more visible in rural areas than in cities. Schools, colleges, institutions, markets and transportation services have been affected across the state,” Das said.He said some relaxation had been given in Bhubaneswar to avoid inconvenience to tourists and people travelling from outside the state. Emergency services were also being allowed to operate.“We are observing the bandh peacefully and following the path of Mahatma Gandhi. There will be no violence,” he said, adding that he had repeatedly appealed to party workers and supporters to maintain peace.Das warned that if the government failed to address the four demands, the agitation would be intensified and could expand significantly over the next two months.  --IANS    ",

Private institutions, business establishments and other establishments in major cities across Odisha also remained closed due to the bandh.</p><div role="region" aria-label="Advertisement" class="hide inside-post-ad filler-ad-unit-inside-post" id="filler_ad"></div><p>Speaking to media persons, Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee (OPCC) president Bhakta Charan Das on Thursday said the 12-hour Odisha bandh called by the INDIA bloc was being observed peacefully across the state, with people extending support to the shutdown.</p><div role="region" aria-label="Advertisement" class="hide inside-post-ad filler-ad-unit-inside-post" id="filler_ad_5"></div><p>Das said the bandh was being observed over four key demands, which include the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, repeal of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, resignation of Odisha School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in textbooks, and immediate relief and compensation for people affected by the recent floods in the state.</p><div role="region" aria-label="Advertisement" class="hide inside-post-ad filler-ad-unit-inside-post" id="filler_ad_6"></div><p>“The impact of the bandh is more visible in rural areas than in cities. Schools, colleges, institutions, markets and transportation services have been affected across the state,” Das said.</p><p>He said some relaxation had been given in Bhubaneswar to avoid inconvenience to tourists and people travelling from outside the state. Emergency services were also being allowed to operate.</p><div role="region" aria-label="Advertisement" class="hide inside-post-ad filler-ad-unit-inside-post" id="filler_ad_7"></div><p>“We are observing the bandh peacefully and following the path of Mahatma Gandhi. There will be no violence,” he said, adding that he had repeatedly appealed to party workers and supporters to maintain peace.</p><div role="region" aria-label="Advertisement" class="hide inside-post-ad filler-ad-unit-inside-post" id="filler_ad_8"></div><p>Das warned that if the government failed to address the four demands, the agitation would be intensified and could expand function setupShareSelection(){
      var topParent = $(".h-share-top-parent");
      topParent.find(".cloned-item").removeClass("cloned-item");

      var topSocialShare = config.topSocialShare || "fb,whatsapp,telegram,twitter"
      var bottomSocialShare = config.bottomSocialShare || "instagram,linkedin,pintrest"
      
      var firstDiv = $(".h-first-div");
      var secondDiv = $(".h-drop-content");
      
      var tArray  = topSocialShare.split(",");
      for(var i=tArray.length-1;i>=0;i--){
        var item = topParent.find("."+tArray[i]+"-anchor");
        if(item.length){
          var itemClone = $(item[0]).clone();
          //- item.remove();
          itemClone.addClass("cloned-item");
          firstDiv.prepend(itemClone);
        }
      }
      var bArray = bottomSocialShare && bottomSocialShare!="-1"  ? bottomSocialShare.split(",") : false;
      if(!bArray){
        secondDiv.remove();
        $(".h-anchor-plus").remove();
      }  else {
        for(var i=bArray.length-1;i>=0;i--){
          var item = topParent.find("."+bArray[i]+"-anchor");
          if(item.length){
            var itemClone = $(item[0]).clone();
            itemClone.addClass("cloned-item");
            secondDiv.prepend(itemClone);
          }
        }
      }
      topParent.find(".social-anchor:not(.cloned-item)").remove();
      
}
function init(){

  if(window.hshare_config){
      $(".h-share-top-parent-wrap").removeClass("hide");
  }
  var config = window.hshare_config || {}
  var hideOnPages = config.hideHSharePages || [];
  if(hideOnPages && hideOnPages.length){
      var pathname = window.location.pathname;
      for(var i=0;i<hideOnPages.length;i++){
          if(pathname==hideOnPages[i]){
              $(".h-share-top-parent-wrap").addClass("hide");
          } 
          if(hideOnPages[i].indexOf("/*")>-1 && hideOnPages[i].indexOf("/*")==hideOnPages[i].length-2){
              var urlt = hideOnPages[i].replace("/*","")
              if(pathname.indexOf(urlt)==0){
                  $(".h-share-top-parent-wrap").addClass("hide");
              }
          }
      }
  }
  setupShareSelection();
  $(window).on('resize', function(){
      setupHShare();
      setupShareSelection();
  });

  var currentShortUrl='';

      if(data && data.element){

          var url = ee.attr("data-url");

          if(shortUrl && window.use_short_url_in_share){

              var index = url.indexOf("/page-");
              url = url.substring(0,index);
          }
      }
  });
  $(".h-share-top-parent-wrap").on("click",".h-anchor a:not(.action-btn),.h-anchor span:not(.action-btn)",function(){

      if(!url){
        url = e.attr("data-url");
      }
      var currUrl = document.URL || window.location.href;
      if(currentShortUrl && currentShortUrl!=currUrl){
        currUrl = currentShortUrl;
      }
      var currTitle = document.title;
      if(currTitle.length>200){
          currTitle = currTitle.substring(0,200);
      }
      if(window.removePageNoFromHShare && currUrl.indexOf("/page-")>-1){
          var index = currUrl.indexOf("/page-");
          currUrl = currUrl.substring(0,index);
      }
      if(!e.hasClass("js-share-article-by-email")){
          url = url.replace("NEWSSTICKYSHAREURL",currUrl);
          url = url.replace("NEWSSTICKYSHARETITLE",encodeURIComponent(currTitle));
          url = url.replace("NEWSSTICKYSHAREURLWITHOUTDOMAIN",window.location.pathname);
          window.open(url, '_blank');
      } else {
          url = url.replace("NEWSSTICKYSHAREURLWITHOUTDOMAIN",window.location.pathname);
          url = url.replace("NEWSSTICKYSHAREURL",document.URL || window.location.href);
          url = url.replace("NEWSSTICKYSHARETITLE",encodeURIComponent(currTitle));
          
          e.attr("data-url-temp",url);
      }
  });
  
}
